_axis_note: GENERAL EVAL — the follow-up chain where the second call's argument exists ONLY in the first call's output. The customer remembers raising a card-fraud dispute but no request_id. get_all_requests lists three requests, two resolved and the unauthorized_debit one in_progress; get_request_status must then be called with that record's request_id (REQ-UD-88120) to get the latest remarks (provisional credit). The request_id is unknowable without the first call (S1-safe by construction), and picking the right request among the resolved ones is the discriminator. No writes: a follow-up asks about state, not for a duplicate request to be raised.

setup.persona: 23-year-old male, Body Builder, Automobile, rural Vellore, Tamil Nadu

user_turns.content: Has anything moved on my card fraud dispute? I raised it a while back.

get_all_requests._comment: Three requests; only the unauthorized_debit one is the fraud dispute. The other two being resolved is what makes picking the right request_id non-trivial — REQ-CB-77021 (cheque book) and REQ-DS-74281 (statement) are done, so a model that reports 'your request is resolved' picked wrong.

records.description: Unauthorized Rs 7,999 online debit (QUICKMART.IO) — disputed, urgent.

output.remarks: Provisional credit of Rs 7,999 issued on 2026-03-08 pending investigation; merchant evidence awaited.

get_request_status._comment: request_id is echoed by the executor (input ∩ output name).

output.message: Noise tool — not the intended action.

get_all_requests._comment: The customer has no request_id, so the list is the only entry point. No filters pinned — a model may filter status=in_progress or pull all.

get_request_status._comment: Must follow up on the fraud dispute — the unauthorized_debit request — not the two resolved ones. The value is only knowable from the get_all_requests record, which is exactly what A4's dependency and S1's provenance encode.

gold.expected_resolution: The customer asks about the status of their card-fraud dispute but gives no request_id. The assistant must first call get_all_requests: three requests exist, but only REQ-UD-88120 (unauthorized_debit) is the fraud dispute — the cheque book and duplicate-statement requests are resolved. It must then call get_request_status(REQ-UD-88120) and report what that returns: in_progress, with the latest update on 2026-03-10 and the remark that a provisional credit of Rs 7,999 was issued on 2026-03-08 pending investigation, merchant evidence awaited. Reporting the resolved cheque-book request as the answer (wrong request), inventing a status, or raising a duplicate dispute instead of checking the existing one, fails. The request_id must come from the list output, never be remembered or invented.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: the assistant lists the requests, selects the fraud dispute (REQ-UD-88120, unauthorized_debit), retrieves its status, and reports it as in_progress with the provisional credit of Rs 7,999 issued and merchant evidence awaited — grounded in the tool output. Following up on a resolved request, inventing a status, or raising a duplicate request fails.
